The destruction of Baoth did not bring freedom. It brought chaos.

For thirty years the collapse was total. No law, no currency, no trade routes. The empire's roads became hunting grounds for bandits. Warlords seized the provinces — former legion commanders, desperate governors, countist lords who had survived the centralization. Warlord Gorvak ruled the north through fear until his own officers cut him down. The Merchant Council of Pilferhorn bought off every army that approached. And in Grimmel, Lady-Protector Selene held the Federation together and opened her gates to every refugee — the Grimmel Refugee Compact, offering sanctuary to anyone fleeing the chaos.

Then the famine came. The granaries were looted, the fields abandoned, the trade routes too dangerous for grain. Between 395 and 370 BGD, an estimated forty percent of central Erisdar starved. Cities of a hundred thousand shrank to ten thousand. The Shadows did not cause the famine — but they made sure no one organized relief. The chaos served their purposes perfectly.

And in the midst of it, around 350 BGD, a woman appeared. She claimed to be the incarnation of the goddess of Discord — the deity who commanded all other gods. She chanted down monsters. She survived assassination. She was reborn three days after her execution. Every miracle was staged. Every monster was planted. She was a homunculus — a Shadow construct passing as human, built to give the dying world a god.

A desperate mother brought her dying child to her, begging for a miracle. Eris looked at the child and said: 'You are not worth it.' That line became infamous — and the Shadows spun it as divine wisdom.

Her teachings were a machine: kill your enemies. Live ascetically. Trust the government. Donate everything to the Church. The chaos made people desperate for any authority — and Eris gave them one answer: the world collapsed because you were sinful. Give everything to me, and you will be saved.

Around 320 BGD she ascended a platform before thousands, delivered her final sermon, and descended into a cave that collapsed behind her. Her body was never found. The cult was self-sustaining now. Within three centuries, the faith of Eris would dominate Erisdar — and the Shadows would have their church.
